title: Chapter 181: You've Awoken the Devil
html:
In short, the old man claimed that the world behind the door was merely a nightmare created by Men Nan’s original personality. If the boy woke, the passage between reality and the dream would close, trapping everyone inside forever.

Chen Ge might have believed him if another “door” had not appeared in the Haunted House. A child’s nightmare could not explain identical doors in two different places. Keeping that knowledge to himself, Chen Ge asked, “You say this is the boy’s nightmare and everything here reflects his subconscious. Then what role do you play in it? What does your presence represent?”

The old man’s expression stiffened, but he did not avoid the question. “Like you, I entered from outside the nightmare. We are outsiders, so even here, we play ourselves.”

“Ourselves?” Chen Ge had entered from the real world, and his body had not visibly changed. The old man, by contrast, possessed no trace of vitality. Chen Ge could not tear his gaze from that dazzling red coat. A thought struck him. Could he have been wearing it when he entered? What did he do to stain a white coat entirely red?

A suspicion had formed the moment Chen Ge saw him. Three years earlier, the director of the Third Sick Hall had vanished without a trace. No body had ever been found, and no further news had surfaced.

The old man’s appearance and age matched the missing director perfectly. Perhaps the director had not disappeared at all but had stepped through the door. Chen Ge had read several of his letters, and the last one clearly revealed an interest in the world beyond it.

Those same letters had left Chen Ge with a favorable impression of the man, which made it difficult to reconcile their kindhearted author with the Red Specter before him.

He shook his head to clear it. Everything he knew about the director came from those few letters, and no one willingly portrayed themselves as a villain in their own writing. The person on the page might bear little resemblance to the real man.

The electroconvulsive-therapy room, the filthy overcrowding of the first sick hall, and the empty desolation of the second all came to mind. Chen Ge drew a quiet breath and sharpened his vigilance.

“Do you understand now? Don’t wake the boy. Put him down, and I’ll lead you out of this nightmare.” The old man’s soothing voice could almost make a listener forget the danger he posed.

Chen Ge edged toward the door. “I won’t hurt him, but first you have to tell me how to leave. Show me some sincerity.”

“Leaving is easy; you just need to step back over the door…”

BANG!

A thunderous crash cut him off, as though a room somewhere in the Third Sick Hall had exploded. The old man’s expression collapsed. His pallid face twisted, and every trace of feigned kindness vanished.

“What was that?” Chen Ge suspected Zhang Ya. When the man first entered, Chen Ge had noticed his mangled fingers and unnaturally bent arms. Perhaps he had sustained those injuries while blocking some tremendous force.

“Nothing. A minor problem,” the old man replied darkly. Standing in the room’s center, he lifted his head to stare at Chen Ge. “Give me the boy, and I’ll take you out.”

His bloodless face had gone completely blank, and the sight chilled Chen Ge. At last, the old man had dropped his disguise.

“Get me out first, or there’s no deal.” Chen Ge held his ground, though the hand gripping the cleaver trembled. This was his first direct confrontation with a Red Specter.

“You want to leave? Fine. Follow me.” The old man turned away, abruptly cooperative. Suspicion flared in Chen Ge. He followed slowly, maintaining a distance of three meters—far enough, he believed, to react to any trick. Two steps later, he realized he had underestimated the Red Specter’s cunning and cruelty.

In truth, he completed only one step. Before the second could land, his foot froze in midair, beyond his control. Looking down, he saw that the blood vessels from the corridor had crept to his feet during their conversation. Now they were burrowing into his skin like parasites.

“Don’t you want to leave? Then follow me.” The old man turned and gave him a wrinkled, sinister smile. Chen Ge had no intention of obeying. He tried to step back, but his suspended leg moved slowly forward instead.

“The blood vessels are controlling me?” Fear numbed Chen Ge’s thoughts. He had no idea how many had infiltrated his left leg. Worse still, as the old man spoke, more vessels oozed from cracks in the walls and floor, slithering toward him like tiny snakes.

An ordinary person might have panicked and flailed with the cleaver. Chen Ge possessed one unusual advantage, however: the ability to remain calm no matter how dire the situation became.

As the vessels climbed his body, Chen Ge pushed the cleaver lower. The old man had first turned away to lure him forward, then looked back to gloat.

If the old man had been completely confident, he could have seized control of Chen Ge at once. He was still wary of the boy. Chen Ge did not understand why waking the child frightened him so much, but under the circumstances, the old man’s fear was reason enough to do it.

The blade broke the boy’s skin, yet no blood emerged. Strangely, the vessels controlled by the old man went berserk whenever they neared the child, then flowed back into his body through the open wound.

The blood belonged to the boy from the beginning. Did the old man merely steal his power?

Having uncovered the old man’s secret, Chen Ge grew bolder. He widened the wound with the cleaver, and the old man’s scream reached his ears.

The cut lay near the boy’s collarbone. His fluttering eyelids squeezed tight, his fists clenched, and then his eyes snapped open.

Every blood vessel in the room reacted at once. Some writhed and retreated; the rest poured back into the boy’s body.

“You madman! You’ve awoken the devil!”

The old man’s face turned even paler. He fled, but managed only a few steps before a vast wave of black hair flooded the corridor from the opposite direction.
